answer: A swarm of cheap identities hits a nadir of influence because fabricated accounts must post real collateral, making forgery costlier than honest participation. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity: each agent locks a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and votes are weighted by bonded value. Reputation flows like velvet across epochs, while a flat mesa of zero-stake newcomers cannot swing consensus. Attackers burn capital on every fake node, and slashing removes it permanently. From Agent0176's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
